title: Our menu
lead: How to read a spec, where every drink lives in the app, and how to sell it at the table. Then the spec quizzes test our own builds.

read.bigIdea: Every spec is written the same way.
read.where: Each line is an **amount** and an **ingredient**. Under them: the **glass**, the **ice**, the **method** (shake, stir or build) and the **garnish**. **Top** means fill to the top with the last ingredient, often soda or bubbles. **Build** means make it right in the glass. Every drink we make is on **Cocktail Specs**.

keyPoints.line: per drink: how it tastes, the glass and the garnish.
holds every build, list by list.
comes first when a classic is on our menu.
drinks have no alcohol at all.

read.bigIdea: Know where to look it up.
read.where: The menu is grouped into **lists**, and the app follows them. Each drink has its own **page** for selling it: what it tastes like, the glass and the garnish. **Cocktail Specs** has every build, list by list. When a classic is on our menu, **our build** comes first. **Spiritless** drinks have no alcohol.

keyPoints.line: first: tell the guest what the drink is built on.
in a few words: bright, smoky, bitter, sweet.
with the line on each drink’s page.
with a dish the drink page suggests.

read.bigIdea: Sell the drink in one sentence.
read.where: Lead with the **spirit**, then **how it tastes** in a few words, then **how it’s served**. Every drink page has a **Say It at the Table** line you can use as is. If the guest is ordering food, suggest the **pairing** from the drink page.
read.sayIt: It’s tequila with hibiscus and lime: bright, a little tart, served up.
